hypothesis: Question: which part of repeated voice measurements actually transfers to motor_UPDRS of unseen patients — between-patient level differences, within-patient fluctuations, or the near-deterministic test_time interpolation trend — and can unlabeled evaluation rows be grouped back into patients so that predictions are pooled at the patient level? Prior measured evidence (baseline losses 8.379 and 8.523 vs 10.465, group MAEs 7.43/7.49 vs 8.91) shows learned models beat the weak reference by only ~20% relative RMSE, which is consistent with two competing explanations: (A) voice features carry a genuine but small cross-patient level signal that is already nearly saturated by a linear/boosted row-wise fit; (B) most of the achievable gain is patient-level (predicting each unseen patient's mean severity), and row-wise models waste capacity on within-patient variation that is largely interpolation noise and not transferable. These make opposite predictions before execution: under (A), per-feature between-patient correlations with patient-mean y will be weak and scattered, oracle patient-level pooling of predictions will barely change RMSE, and row-held-out CV will roughly match patient-held-out CV; under (B), y variance will be dominated by the between-patient component, oracle pooling of the same predictions will noticeably cut RMSE and group MAE, and row-held-out CV will be markedly optimistic relative to GroupKFold. A third, decision-critical unknown is whether patient identity is recoverable transductively from the unlabeled input matrix (age/sex plus stable voice profile, excluding test_time); if agglomerative clustering recovers dev patients with high ARI/purity and pooling by cluster approaches oracle pooling, a patient-pooling wrapper becomes a legitimate method for later rounds, otherwise pooling must be abandoned and effort should go to shrinkage of row-wise predictions toward the train mean. This action is an analysis (no prediction), it uses only the train and development data supplied to analyze, it reports metrics computed on those splits, and any clustering of unlabeled rows is explicitly labeled transductive. It is exploratory: the numbers, not the narrative, decide the next round.
